# PRIMAL2 comparison harness

`run_our_instances.py` runs PRIMAL2 on the instances of this repository under the
same task semantics as every other comparison method: one task per agent, the
agent disappears from the world the step it first reaches its sink, and no
stay-at-goal. It uses PRIMAL2's own `isOneShot` branch in `MAPFEnv.step_all`
rather than reimplementing removal. `README_ours.md` documents every deviation
from stock PRIMAL2 and the acceptance tests that were run.

The file is vendored here because it is our contribution and it must be
versioned with the experiments that cite it, while upstream PRIMAL2 belongs to a
third party we cannot push to. `results/revision_final/frozen_artifacts_step_v2/MANIFEST.json`
pins it by sha256 `1ec65f09…d92ee5`, which is the copy in this directory.

## Getting a working environment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/marmotlab/PRIMAL2.git
cd PRIMAL2
cp /path/to/lima/third_party/primal2/run_our_instances.py .
cp /path/to/lima/third_party/primal2/README_ours.md .
```

Then follow `README_ours.md`. In short: a conda environment on Python 3.7 with
TensorFlow 1.15 and protobuf pinned at or below 3.20.3, `od_mstar3` compiled in
place, and the official one-shot checkpoint.

Two things are deliberately **not** in git.

- **The model checkpoint** (`model_primal2_oneshot/`, 385 MB) comes from the
  official PRIMAL2 Dropbox release. Results only reproduce with the same
  checkpoint, so copy the directory rather than retraining.
- **`od_mstar3/cython_od_mstar.cpp`** is regenerated by Cython during the build
  and differs by thousands of lines between machines. Build it, do not copy it.

## What this harness is for

It is the only supported way to run PRIMAL2 on our maps and scenarios. Do not
invoke PRIMAL2's own driver scripts for comparison numbers, because they use
different task semantics and a different goal representation.
